title: Perf run 20261016-0821
heading: No speed change this run: dead CSS removed, five checks that could not fail now can, and a slower join traced to the labels' new type
meta: This run made the game no faster and no slower. Against main b455e10, the final code (3b73fe5) has no headline row called better or worse in 4 pairs, and memory is unchanged. The PR removes 47 lines of the app's CSS that never applied, adds a console warning when a game's record can't be replayed, and makes five tests and lint rules able to fail on the faults they name. The run also found that the shared game's first screen got about 21% slower in the bench when the labels started being centred by their capital letters (#155). No fix that keeps that look was found, so the question is yours (below).

items.title: Keep the labels' new type although the shared game's first screen is slower in the bench?
items.body:
#155 centres every label by the height of its capital letters. In the bench, the commit that did it made the Join button on a shared game's page appear 21% later (89.6 → 114 ms, 8 pairs), and the joiner's first board picture 8.8% later (7 of 8 pairs worse). On main as it is now, the Join button is 23% later in 6 pairs. When the browser records a trace of each join, the gap shrinks to 3.1%, and a separate probe saw only 3–6%. So the bench shows a real but uneven cost, mostly in the second game a browser joins, and I could not name the work behind it.

Two things were tried without keeping the look and gave no wall-time change in the probe: dropping the cap unit, and dropping text-box. No player-facing change is in this PR.

items.recommend: Keep the look. The cost is under 25 ms on a screen that appears once per game, it is smaller in every measurement made without the bench's back-to-back joins, and the type is a deliberate design choice. Say so if you want the old label alignment back instead.

items.title: Two headline rows lean slower on the final code; merge anyway?
items.body:
The skill asks me to list any headline row more than 3% slower at the median, even when the comparison does not call it. Two are:

  • The joiner's first board picture: +20% in 4 pairs (1.40 1.16 1.02 1.26), then +6.6% in 8 more (5 of 8 slower).
  • Reopening a long game: +18% in 4 pairs, then +19% in 8 (pairs 0.87 to 2.24). Its first step, the server's answer arriving, is +26%, and that happens before any of the page's code runs.

To see how far identical code drifts, I compared the final code with itself, 8 pairs. It gave the joiner's picture +7.5%, the shared game's page +15% (7 of 8 pairs slower), and reopening −7.6%. The branch changes no code these rows run: it deletes CSS declarations that never applied and adds a warning that only prints when a record fails to replay.

scoreboard.intro:
The headline rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. On the final code 3b73fe5 against main b455e10, 4 pairs: 0.982 times as fast over the 14 rows, none called better or worse (identical code compared with itself gives about 1.004). JavaScript memory on a reopened long game is +0.0%; geometries grown over 16 moves stay at 10 and textures at 0. Three rows that leaned slower were run again with 8 pairs: the player's own move went from +6.7% to −2.2%; the other two are under Needs from me.

At the start of the run, main b455e10 against the last run's base 1a04c29 was 1.024 times as fast over the 14 rows, none called. The one lead, the shared game's first screen (+24% in 8 pairs, 7 slower), was bisected to #155 (Needs from me).

This run did not measure against the first recorded run (92ce041), because no change here was meant to change speed. The last run's figure stands: e02a235 was 2.48 times as fast as 92ce041 over the 11 headline rows both can measure, against a target of 1.2. The chart below is that comparison.

items.title: A record that can't be replayed now says why (debc150)
items.body: When a game's saved moves could not be replayed, the page showed that the record stopped, and nothing said which move or why. The console now gets one warning with the move and the error. A test checks the exact message.

items.title: Five checks that passed on broken code now fail on it
items.body:
• The notation test for two pieces of different kinds now uses a rook that can actually reach the square, so deleting the kind filter fails it (b861ff5).
  • The rim test now counts every layout read at attach, height and computed style included (4f653b3).
  • The HUD fit test now fails when the turn pill is not measured during a game, where it used to pass without checking (5f36510).
  • A new history test fails if a landing move copies the earlier moves' notation instead of keeping it (006c6d1).
  • A new test fails when a stylesheet reads a custom property, without a fallback, that nothing sets (f0f96ee, c13f805). It found one: --hud-check-ink, read since #73 and never defined.

items.title: Rules that were only written down are now checked
items.body:
• The focus lint (use focusFromCode, not a bare .focus()) now covers the scene and the canvases, which had their own lint blocks without it (119c641).
  • The start page's 12 pictures are checked against the sizes the lens code expects (f1fcd75).
  • bench/loop/.gitignore admits only the files the loop may commit (b6c2991).

items.title: The bench says more
items.body: The review section waits up to 10 s for its button and says what it waited for (3903aaf). A canvas that never came to rest before a timed action is counted and reported (f1e9148). Each join can be traced on demand with BENCH_TRACE_JOIN, and a probe for the shared game's first screen is in bench/loop/tools/join-probe/ (ebef251, 3b73fe5).

removed.intro: Against main, outside bench/loop/, the branch adds 153 lines and removes 82 in 11 files. The app's own code shrinks by 47 lines: −47 in index.css (28 plain sizes that a later rule in the same block always replaced, the play pill's sizes that .lobby-go always overrides, the never-coloured .lobby-error, and a reduced-motion animation: none with no animation left to stop), −2 in ChooseSide.tsx, and +2 for the warning in history.ts. Tests grow by 82 lines, the bench by 33, and the lint config by 3. The one visible-in-principle deletion, a taller play pill in tall windows, never applied: .lobby-go always won the cascade.

items.title: A fix for the slower join that keeps #155's look
items.body: Builds without the cap unit, and without text-box, moved no wall time in the probe. Parked for you (Needs from me).

items.title: A faster test for ambiguous moves in the notation
items.body: Replaying the bench's 2,000-move game under node takes 6.8 ms, and 3.4 ms with the ambiguity test removed altogether. That is at most about 3% of reopening a long game, below what the bench can call, for about 30 new lines of engine code. Not tried in the app.

items.title: One component for a move as the move list says it
items.body: It saved no lines, and its first version formatted each move once more per render, which the move list's count test caught. Reverted.

choices.intro:
• The regression check ran against the last run's base (1a04c29), not its bookmark, so that it covered the five PRs main took during the last run.
  • .lobby-error had never been coloured. I deleted the rule rather than make the error red, because red would change what a player sees.
  • The play pill's taller size in tall windows had never applied. I deleted it rather than make it apply.
  • Only the RG6 A/B reports are committed; the probe's traces and timings stay out of git, and the record calls its figures exploratory.
  • Six of the diff reviewers' smaller findings went into the ledger instead of the PR (CF1, CG1, HW1, SV1, AV1, BU1); three were fixed here.

notConfirmed.intro:
• That the CSS deletions change nothing on screen rests on reading the cascade and on one-off comparisons of the parsed and computed styles in Chromium, which are not committed. No screenshot pair was made.
  • Why the second join in a browser is slower after #155. The probe and the traced bench disagree with the untraced bench on its size.
  • That the capital-sized buttons keep their size in browsers without mod(), round() or the cap unit (Chrome before 125, Safari before 17.2). Read in the source, not loaded in such a browser (ledger CF1).

next.intro:
1. Find the bench's pair-order offset: identical code leans 7–15% on the setup rows (1016:AA1).
  2. Give the capital-sized boxes a fallback for older browsers (1016-0821:CF1).
  3. Count the first click's two modes instead of timing a median (1009-1606:Q1).
  4. Run on-page searches one at a time when a worker fails to load (1015:RV17).
  5. Place the phone's start-page picture before the entry runs (1015:SP4).
  6. A year's cache for /assets/*, with a warm-load case in the bench (0930:17).
